title: Barghawata Conference
capsule: The Barghawata were a Berber tribal confederation of the Masmuda group occupying the Atlantic coastal plain of Morocco (Tamesna) between Safi and Salé, who emerged in the mid-eighth century in the wake of the Sufri Kharijite rebellion against Umayyad rule. Under Salih ibn Tarif and his successors they developed a syncretic religion blending Islam with indigenous Berber custom, including a Berber-language 'Quran' and distinctive food taboos. The confederation held out against multiple Almoravid assaults—Abdallah ibn Yasin died fighting them in 1058—before being politically and religiously eliminated by the Almohads around 1149.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general location of Barghawata territory is established by medieval Arab geographers, but precise boundaries of the confederation at any given century are poorly mapped and largely inferential.
